overview.history: The Entertainer is ready to explore on Lune. It is associated with Scott Joplin. Stylistically it sits in the 20th Century world. Start by listening, then ask about the bars that surprise your hands. Ragtime strides in the left hand — keep that bounce steady under a cheeky right hand.

composerInfo.name: Scott Joplin
composerInfo.hook: Joplin’s rags stride and sparkle — steady left hand, cheeky right hand.
composerInfo.bio: Dubbed the "King of Ragtime", he composed more than 40 ragtime pieces, one ragtime ballet, and two operas. One of his first and most popular pieces, the "Maple Leaf Rag", became the genre's first and most influential hit, later being recognized as the quintessential rag. Joplin considered ragtime to be a form of classical music meant to be played in concert halls and largely disdained the performance of ragtime as honky tonk music most common in saloons.
composerInfo.full: Scott Joplin was an American composer and pianist. Dubbed the "King of Ragtime", he composed more than 40 ragtime pieces, one ragtime ballet, and two operas. One of his first and most popular pieces, the "Maple Leaf Rag", became the genre's first and most influential hit, later being recognized as the quintessential rag. Joplin considered ragtime to be a form of classical music meant to be played in concert halls and largely disdained the performance of ragtime as honky tonk music most common in saloons.
highlights: Joplin is closely tied to the piano — tone and touch are part of the story.

chapters.title: About Scott Joplin
chapters.body: Scott Joplin was an American composer and pianist. Dubbed the "King of Ragtime", he composed more than 40 ragtime pieces, one ragtime ballet, and two operas. One of his first and most popular pieces, the "Maple Leaf Rag", became the genre's first and most influential hit, later being recognized as the quintessential rag. Joplin considered ragtime to be a form of classical music meant to be played in concert halls and largely disdained the performance of ragtime as honky tonk music most common in saloons.
